title: Terraform module: internal ingress chain with L7 TLS termination and AZ-aware failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a reusable Terraform module that implements a two-tier internal ingress chain (NLB -> ALB) for Private/VPC deployments. The module should provide a configurable, production-ready template for: 1) fronting private clusters with an NLB in passthrough mode for IP/port preservation and cross-AZ balancing, 2) an internal ALB for L7 routing and TLS termination (SNI-aware), and 3) clear health check semantics and a failover policy that prefers healthy AZs to minimize cross-AZ connection churn.

Goals:
- Provide a single module that operators can enable with variables rather than composing multiple low-level modules.
- Support both TLS termination at ALB and TLS passthrough to backends via NLB (toggleable).
- Ensure health checks are explicit and safe for stateful backends (avoid aggressive drain thresholds).
- Implement AZ-aware failover: when a target group's AZ becomes unhealthy, traffic should route to healthy AZs gracefully and trigger playback metrics.
- Export Terraform outputs and IAM roles necessary for automation and monitoring.

Scope & Non-goals:
- Scope: internal/private ingress only (no public internet ALB). Includes target groups, listeners, cert attachments, security groups, route53 private records, and cloudwatch alarms.
- Non-goal: replacing customer-managed edge proxies; module should integrate with existing Envoy ingress if provided.

Design decisions made so far:
- Use NLB TCP listener with preserved source IP in front; it provides lowest cost cross-AZ balancing and keeps client IP for backend auth.
- ALB internal sits behind NLB and performs TLS termination by default. ALB listener rules are path/SNI-aware.
- TLS certs: allow two modes: (a) ALB-managed ACM cert attached to ALB; (b) NLB passthrough with backend-managed certs when customers require end-to-end TLS. Mode selected via variable "tls_mode" = ["alb", "passthrough"].
- Health checks: ALB target groups use HTTP/HTTPS health checks hitting /_internal/healthz with 10s interval and 3 consecutive successes. NLB target group uses TCP health check with 10s interval. Provide variables to tune these.
- Draining & connection draining: implement target group deregistration delay of 90s by default to allow graceful session completion for stateful workloads.
- AZ-aware routing: leverage target group weighting and CloudWatch alarms to shift traffic. On sustained AZ-level degradation, Terraform runtime won't move traffic at apply-time; instead, emit CloudWatch metrics and provide an automation hook (SNS -> Lambda) to adjust weights. Documented as recommended pattern.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module deploys in a test VPC and provisions NLB and ALB with correct listener rules within 30 minutes.
- TLS termination at ALB with ACM cert succeeds; ALB returns correct certificate when SNI matches.
- When ALB target in one AZ is made unhealthy, traffic is routed to healthy AZs with <150ms additional latency in steady state.
- Health check metrics and alarms are created and visible in Console.
- Module exposes outputs: nlb_dns, alb_dns, target_group_arns, listener_arns, cloudwatch_alarm_names.

Implementation plan / tasks:
- Module skeleton and variables: create inputs for tls_mode, backend_port, health_path, deregistration_delay, enable_sticky (default false), az_balance_threshold. (2d)
- Networking & SGs: create security groups for ALB->targets and NLB listeners; default deny inbound except by VPC CIDR and monitor subnets. (1d)
- NLB configuration: dual-stack support, cross-zone enabled by default. (1d)
- ALB configuration: internal scheme, listener and rule generation from list of path->target mapping. (2d)
- Health checks & alarms: create target group health checks and CloudWatch alarms + SNS topic for automation hooks. (1d)
- Tests & examples: one minimal example and one with passthrough and mTLS backend. Include terratest cases for provisioning and health-check failover. (2d)
- Docs & runbook: usage notes, rollout strategy, rollback steps, and known limitations. (1d)

Rollout / Rollback plan:
- Canary: deploy module to staging VPC, validate with synthetic traffic. Next, enable module in one non-critical customer VPC behind an existing edge proxy. Run for 48h with increased monitoring.
- Rollback: reverse terraform apply to previous module version, or flip tls_mode to previous setting. Drain targets and confirm session completion before removing ALB.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we support per-listener ALB WAF integration by default? Left as opt-in variable since WAF adds cost and policy complexity.
- Automated weight adjustment in Terraform is not ideal; we propose providing an automation hook (SNS -> Lambda) rather than baking dynamic traffic shifting into the module.

Notes on compatibility with Private deployments and Dedicated clusters:
- Module assumes API access to ACM and Route53 in customer's account. For on-prem deployments, the module provides outputs that can be translated into private DNS records.

Acceptance test playbook (high level):
1) Apply module in test VPC.
2) Attach ALB ACM cert and verify SNI routing to different hostnames.
3) Mark one AZ's targets unhealthy and measure failover.
4) Validate deregistration_delay behavior with long-lived TCP connections.
